extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive procedural standards from the MPEP governing conduct, timing, filings, responses, extensions of time, and treatment of submissions in USPTO ex parte reexamination proceedings. Focuses on what is required of patent owners, third party requesters, and examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal and mailing of Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions and identifying information must be printed and mailed to the patent owner’s legal representative (or the patent owner if no representative). Only the first patent owner’s address is printed where multiple owners exist. All actions in a third party requester ex parte reexamination must have a copy mailed to the third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A completed transmittal form PTOL-465 is provided for each partial patent owner and for any third party requester. The number of PTOL-465 forms corresponds to the number of copies to be mailed; the form permits use of window envelopes. A transmittal form PTOL-465 must be used when providing the third party requester with a copy of each Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time — general rule (37 CFR 1.550(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for any action by a patent owner in an ex parte reexamination will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified; a request must be filed on or before the day action is due and must be accompanied by the petition fee under § 1.17(g). Mere filing of a request does not effect an extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extension are decided by the Director of the CRU or Technology Center conducting the reexamination and will be granted only for sufficient cause. Requests filed before the decision to grant/deny reexamination will be denied. The Director evaluates sufficient cause in light of providing the patent owner a fair opportunity to present arguments and the statutory requirement that reexamination be conducted with special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 305). Certificates of mailing/transmission and Express Mail procedures (37 CFR 1.8, 1.10) may be used to file extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content required in an extension request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of time must fully state the reasons for the extension, including what actions the patent owner has taken to date and why, despite those actions, additional time is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must provide a factual accounting demonstrating reasonably diligent behavior by all those responsible for preparing the response. Requests must be submitted in a separate paper and include the petition fee. Requests to extend the time to file a petition from denial of reexamination are entertained only via a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 with appropriate fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for statutory periods and third party replies (no extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory periods set by Congress cannot be extended; specifically, the 2-month period for a third party requester reply under 37 CFR 1.535 (and 35 U.S.C. 304) cannot be extended under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory period for response cannot be waived. See MPEP § 2251. Other statutory timing (e.g., filing notices of appeal or commencing civil actions) is governed by appropriate CFR provisions (e.g., 37 CFR 1.304).

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final automatic 1-month extension practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a timely first response to a final rejection having a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the shortened period for an additional month; the period for response may not exceed six months from the date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This automatic 1-month extension applies only to the first response to the final rejection (even informal or unsigned). The primary examiner is authorized to grant this implicit extension. The automatic extension does not apply once a Notice of Appeal has been filed. If the advisory action cannot be mailed in time, the examiner may grant additional time and state the extension in the advisory Office action (PTOL-467); the blank for months must be filled with an integer (2–6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies and responses requirement (37 CFR 1.111) — specificity and bona fide attempt
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is adverse, the patent owner must reply and request reconsideration or further examination. The reply must be reduced to writing and must distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors in the examiner’s action and reply to every ground of objection and rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. General allegations that claims are patentable without specific distinctions do not comply. Amendments in reply must clearly point out the patentable novelty and how amendments avoid cited references or objections. The reply must appear throughout to be a bona fide attempt to advance the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies — limits on entry (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply to a compliant reply will not be entered as a matter of right except where clearly limited to specific matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may enter a supplemental reply only if it is clearly limited to: (A) cancellation of claims; (B) adoption of examiner suggestions; (C) placement of the proceeding in condition for allowance (or NIRC); (D) reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply; (E) correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); or (F) simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply filed during a period when action is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c) will be entered. If not entered, the contents must be included in a proper response to a subsequent Office action to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.550)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexaminations must be conducted with special dispatch; patent owners are given at least 30 days to respond to any Office action; responses may include statements and/or proposed amendments or new claims to place the patent in condition where all claims, if amended as proposed, would be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response (or required interview summary) prosecution will be terminated and a reexamination certificate issued under § 1.570 per the last Office action. Late responses may be excused only under petition provisions of 37 CFR 1.137(a) (unavoidable delay) or 1.137(b) (unintentional delay). Documents filed must be served on the other party per § 1.248 or may be refused consideration. The reexamination requester will receive copies of Office actions; requester’s active participation ends after the reply under § 1.535. Third-party submissions after the date of order must meet § 1.501(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on patent owner submitting third-party papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owners must not file papers on behalf of any third party; if a third party paper is included with a timely patent owner response, the entire submission is improper and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If returned, the third party paper will not be considered. The decision returning the improper submission should provide an appropriate extension under 37 CFR 1.550(c) to refile the patent owner response without the third party paper. See MPEP §§ 2254 and 2267.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) not permitted in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An ADS cannot be submitted in a reexamination proceeding because a reexamination is not an 'application' (see 37 CFR 1.76); an ADS is an improper paper in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners should not attempt to use ADS filings to effect application-like changes in reexamination files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submission — definition and examiner options (MPEP §2266.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner submission is 'not fully responsive' to a non-final Office action where: (A) a bona fide response is filed; (B) before expiration of the response period; and (C) through oversight or inadvertence some point necessary to a full response has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these conditions are met, prosecution should not be terminated; the examiner may (A) waive minor deficiencies and act on the submission; (B) accept the amendment as a response but notify the patent owner via a new Office action setting a new time period to supply the omission; or (C) notify the patent owner to complete the response within the remaining period for response (or any extension) to avoid termination. Serious deficiencies or insufficient time justify issuing a new time period (usually 1 month). Form paragraph 22.14 may be used to notify patent owner. The practice applies only for inadvertent omissions, not deliberate omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of omissions and timing pre- vs post-final
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an inadvertent omission occurs in a pre-final bona fide response, the examiner may give time to supply the omission; after final rejection an advisory Office action (PTOL-467) should be issued to explain the omission and the filing of the first timely response after final triggers the automatic 1‑month extension (see MPEP §2265).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practice of giving time to supply an omission does not apply after a final Office action for amendments that would not place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate. Amendments filed after final are approved for entry only if they place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate or are in better form for appeal; otherwise they are denied entry. If an amendment filed after final would place the proceeding in condition except for an omission through inadvertence, the examiner should consider withdrawing the final action and issuing a new action or entering the amendment where appropriate (Ex parte Quayle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal or defective submissions and notice (MPEP §2266.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even complete submissions can be defective (informal). Examples of defects include: (A) no proof of service; (B) unsigned paper; (C) signed by a person not of record; (D) amendment not complying with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) amendment not complying with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-475 is used to notify of defects; appropriate boxes can be checked and blanks filled. If further clarification is needed (e.g., specifics of why amendment does not comply), attach a separate sheet. If the defect is not listed, use the 'other' box and explain. Some procedural examples: submission on easily erasable paper would be defective and require a new submission.
